source_text: Καὶ πρῶτον μὲν τὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου πανδημεὶ σωρηδὸν ἐπιφερόμενα γενναίως ὑπέμενον, ἐπιβοήσεις καὶ πληγὰς καὶ συρμοὺς καὶ διαρπαγὰς καὶ λίθων βολὰς καὶ συγκλείσεις καὶ πάνθ᾽ ὅσα ἠγριωμένῳ πλήθει ὡς πρὸς ἐχθροὺς καὶ πολεμίους φιλεῖ γίνεσθαι, καὶ δὴ ἀναχθέντες εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν ὑπό τε τοῦ χιλιάρχου καὶ τῶν προεστηκότων τῆς πόλεως ἐξουσιῶν ἐπὶ παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους ἀνακριθέντες καὶ ὁμολογήσαντες, συνεκλείσθησαν εἰς τὴν εἱρκτὴν ἕως τῆς τοῦ ἡγεμόνος παρουσίας.
pass_a_gloss: And as a first matter, they nobly held firm under the things being inflicted on them from the mob, by the whole people together, in heaps — outcries and blows and draggings and tearings-asunder and castings of stones and shuttings-up and all whatever things tend to be done by an enraged multitude toward enemies and hostile opponents — and indeed, after being led up into the marketplace and, before the whole multitude, being examined by both the chiliarch and the ruling authorities of the city and having confessed, they were shut together into the prison until the presence of the governor.
pass_b_english: First, they nobly bore everything the crowd heaped on them all at once: shouts and blows, dragging and tearing, volleys of stones and shuttings-up — everything an enraged mob does to enemies and foes. Then they were led up into the marketplace, questioned before the whole crowd by the military tribune and the city magistrates, and after confessing, they were shut together in prison until the governor arrived.

lemmas.gloss: endured, held out under suffering here
enraged, made savage, of the multitude

choices.english: inflicted on them by the whole people together in a mass
choices.why: both adverbs modify the participle and stress collective, heaped action from the crowd, so rendered as manner plus agent rather than two detached adverbs
imperfect with adverb of noble bearing describes sustained brave endurance under attack, not a single act of patience
context is a civic examination in the marketplace alongside city magistrates, so the office is the Roman commander rather than a generic captain
